## Before submitting

- [x] I agree to license this contribution under the terms of [LICENSE.txt](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/blob/develop/LICENSE.txt).
- [x] I ran `pre-commit run` and committed any formatting changes.
- [x] I reviewed the Hard Rules in the `AGENTS.md` for each directory this PR touches (see [root AGENTS.md § Reviewing a PR](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/blob/develop/AGENTS.md#reviewing-a-pr-human-or-agent)) and my changes comply, or I explain the exception below.
- [x] I added GitHub labels: one `cat-*`, one or more `area:*` / `op:*`, and one `orig-*` (see [label list](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/labels)).

## Affected area

Packaging (Python wheel)

## Summary

**Release 1.31: please cherry-pick into `1.31.0-rc`.** The change applies unchanged there.

`kda_hopper_cuda` is the KDA engine ranked first on SM90. At run time it reads and NVRTC-compiles `python/cudnn/linear_attention/hopper/cuda_kernels/kda_{fused,bwd}_sm90.cu` (`hopper/cuda_host.py`, `hopper/cuda_bwd_host.py`). No `[tool.setuptools.package-data]` glob lists those files, and package discovery only collects `.py`. So the 1.30.0 wheel and the 1.31.0 candidate ship without them, and the engine raises `FileNotFoundError` from an installed wheel. The CAKE kernels next to them were already listed.

**Fix.** Add `"cudnn.linear_attention.hopper" = ["cuda_kernels/*.cu"]`.

**Tripwire.** The new `test/python/core/test_package_data.py` asserts that every non-Python, non-Markdown file under `python/cudnn` is matched by a package-data glob. It fails on the base with exactly these two files.

## Testing

| Check | Base (`1.31.0-rc`) | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| `setup.py build_py` output contains `hopper/cuda_kernels/*.cu` | no | yes (both files) |
| `cuda_host._library(0)` on H100, from the `build_py` tree (installed layout) | `FileNotFoundError: .../hopper/cuda_kernels/kda_fused_sm90.cu` | loads |
| `core/test_package_data.py` | fails, listing the two `.cu` files | passes |

Why CI did not catch this: under the repo's pytest setup, `cudnn` resolves to the installed tree but `cudnn.linear_attention.hopper.cuda_host` resolves to the source tree. So `test_bdist_wheels` reads the kernels from the checkout. I verified this by printing `cudnn.__file__` and `cuda_host.__file__` inside pytest. The direct probe above runs outside pytest.

detail.title: [Auto-FE] Ship the SM90 KDA CUDA kernel sources in the wheel (1.31 cherry-pick)

files.patch:
@@ -0,0 +1,47 @@
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright (c) 2026 NVIDIA CORPORATION & AFFILIATES. All rights reserved.
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+
+"""Every non-Python file shipped under python/cudnn is listed in pyproject's package-data.
+
+Package discovery only collects ``.py`` files; anything read at run time (NVRTC
+kernel sources, checksums, vendored licenses) reaches a wheel only through a
+``[tool.setuptools.package-data]`` glob. A missing glob passes every in-tree run
+and fails only for wheel users: the SM90 KDA CUDA engine shipped without its
+``.cu`` sources and raised FileNotFoundError from an installed wheel.
+"""
+
+from pathlib import Path
+
+import pytest
+
+pytestmark = pytest.mark.L0
+
+_REPO = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]
+_PKG_ROOT = _REPO / "python"
+# Not package data: sources, their bytecode, docs, and the extension built in place.
+_NOT_DATA = {".py", ".pyc", ".md", ".so", ".pyd"}
+
+
+def _package_data():
+    try:
+        import tomllib
+    except ModuleNotFoundError:  # Python 3.10
+        tomllib = pytest.importorskip("tomli")
+    pyproject = _REPO / "pyproject.toml"
+    if not pyproject.is_file():
+        pytest.skip("needs the source tree (pyproject.toml)")
+    with pyproject.open("rb") as f:
+        return tomllib.load(f)["tool"]["setuptools"].get("package-data", {})
+
+
+def test_every_runtime_data_file_is_package_data():
+    covered = set()
+    for package, patterns in _package_data().items():
+        if not package.startswith("cudnn"):
+            continue
+        package_dir = _PKG_ROOT / package.replace(".", "/")
+        for pattern in patterns:
+            covered.update(p.resolve() for p in package_dir.glob(pattern) if p.is_file())
+    shipped = [p.resolve() for p in (_PKG_ROOT / "cudnn").rglob("*") if p.is_file() and p.suffix not in _NOT_DATA and "__pycache__" not in p.parts]
+    missing = sorted(str(p.relative_to(_PKG_ROOT)) for p in shipped if p not in covered)
+    assert not missing, f"add these to [tool.setuptools.package-data] in pyproject.toml: {missing}"
